chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Mismāʿ, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled regarding the fingernail: if it is cut off and does not grow back, or it comes out black and damaged, then the compensation is ten dinars. But if it comes out white, then it is five dinars.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ: title of Imam Ali عليه السلام as the Commander of the Faithful
key_terms.ٱلظُّفُرِ: the fingernail; the injured body part under discussion

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah for a fingernail that is cut off and does or does not regrow properly in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling from Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام concerning compensation for injury to a fingernail. The amount of diyah differs according to the resulting harm: fuller compensation is due when the nail does not regrow or regrows damaged, and lesser compensation when it regrows in a healthier state.
